Date July 28, 1931

Subject (in full) Attempted Communist Demonstration of July 22, 1931.

Made by and Forwarded by D. I. Ross

In connection with the information supplied
by Western Agent in his report of July 22, regarding proposed
communist demonstrations in Central and Hongkew Districts
on the evening of July 22, which resulted in the apprehension
of eleven demonstrators, the seizure of a quantity of
communistic literature and the possible prevention of
serious incidents, as two of the persons arrested were found
to be in possession of a number of stones while on the
person of a third was found a 'Blown' egg filled with
a white substance, believed to be lime, I beg to recommend
that this Agent in recognition of his timely information
be granted a monetary reward in the sum of $25. from the
Crime Suppression Fund.

D. I.
Officer i/c Special Branch.

H. C. (Brine)
I wish to endorse the
above recommendation.

J. P. Swiens

The following is a list of communistic pamphlets seized
by Nanking Station on Broadway between 7.35 p.m. and 7.50 p.m.
July 31st 1931.

1. Pamphlet bearing slogans denouncing the Kuomintang
and demanding freedom of publication and assembly.
2. Manifesto issued by the Communist Youth League
urging the young men to oppose the Japanese imperial- X
ism in connection with the Wanpaoshan incidents.
3. Pamphlet bearing slogans opposing Japanese imperial-
ism in connection with the Wanpaoshan incidents. X
4. Manifesto bearing slogans congratulating the Red Army
on its success.
5. Pamphlet bearing slogans calling for the support of
Soviet Russia.
6. Manifesto issued by the Shanghai Eastern District
Committee of the Chinese Communist Party, calling
for the opposition of Japanese imperialists in X
connection with the Wanpaoshan incidents.
7. Song dedicated to the victory of the Red Army in
Kiangsi.
8. Manifesto issued by the Eastern District Committee
of the Chinese Communist Party relating to the
Hoover War Debt Moratorium.
9. Manifesto issued by the Chpai District Committee of
the Chinese Communist Youth League, calling for the
demonstrations in connection with the execution of
Shiang Tsang Fah ( ).
10. Manifesto issued by the Shanghai Eastern District of
the Chinese Communist Party, calling upon the workers
to commemorate August 1st.
11. Manifesto issued by the Shanghai Eastern District
Committee of the Chinese Communist Party congratulating
the successes attained by the Red Army during the Third

Kuomintang Suppression Period .
12. Manifesto issued by the Eastern District Committee of
Chinese Communist Party calling upon labourers to
commemorate August 1st.
13. Multifarious Pamphlet bearing slogans calling upon masses
to congratulate the success attained by the Red Army
and to support the Soviet Russia.
14. Manifesto issued by the Central Committee of the Chinese
Communist Youth League to Korean youth in connection with
the Wanpaoshan case.

July 22, 1931.

D. 2607
* See
D. 2607 A.

It is reported that Communists are planning
to distribute Red literature in the Central and Hongkew
districts between 6.30 p.m. and 8 p.m. July 22. It is
proposed that the demonstrators will first assemble at
the corner of Peking Road and the Bund where they will be
given further orders by a man carrying a small round
basket in the front of a bicycle. It is said that the
parties arranging the demonstration have the following
purposes in view :-
1. To inform the public about the victories of the "Red"
Armies in Kiangsi.
2. To emphasize the disapproval of the public of the
execution of Hsiang Chung-fa.
3. To prepare the public for the celebrations on August 1,
International Red Day, and August 20, the anniversary
of the assassination of Liao Chung-kai.

July 22
at Date 22 - 7 - 31 19 31）

Subject (in full) Proposed Communist Demonstration.

Made by D. I. Kuh Pao-hwa Forwarded by （签名）

Sir,
Agent reports that a number of local communists
consisting of students and workers are planning to hold
a demonstration between 6.30 and 8 p.m. July 22 in
commemoration of the victories of the Red Army in
Kiangsi, the execution of Shiang Tsong-fah and to
further propaganda with the object of utilising
the approaching anniversary of the death of Liao Chung-kai,
a prominent member of the Kuomintang Party and the
Canton Government, who was assassinated in Canton on
August 20, 1925.

It is reported that the demonstrators will
assemble at The Bund and Peking Roads corner, after
which they will proceed in small groups, disseminating
communistic literature north along The Bund towards
Hongkew District. They will be led by a man riding
a bicycle carrying a small, round basket suspended
in front of the machine.

Kuh Pao-hwa
D. I.
Officer i/c Special Branch.

Commissioner of Police,
Sir,
（批：Information. The substance of
the above report will be included in the Daily
Summary sent to Divisions and Districts on
July 22, to-day.
M. Sweno
O. i/c Sp. Br.
22:7:31.）

（左侧边缘手写批注：RWM 2/7）

Sir,

The proposed meeting mention-
ed in the attached report, supposed
to be held on July 7, did not take
